preconditions.description: The input consists of two integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^9) and m (0 ≤ m ≤ 4), where n is the number of nodes in the complete binary tree and m is the number of extra undirected edges added.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and 1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(v) <= n and int(u) != int(v) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1+m])
preconditions.description: Each of the m extra edges is represented by two distinct integers u and v (1 ≤ u, v ≤ n, u ≠ v), where u and v are the endpoints of the edge.
The complete binary tree structure is implicitly defined: node 1 is the root, and the parent of node i (2 ≤ i ≤ n) is floor(i/2).

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == sum(1 for length in range(1, n+1) for path in all_simple_paths(n, m, stdin) if len(path) == length) % (10**9 + 7)
postconditions.description: The output is the total number of simple paths in the graph (including single-node paths), modulo 10^9 + 7, where a simple path is a sequence of distinct nodes connected by edges (undirected, possibly multiple) without repetition.

postconditions.expression: all_simple_paths(n, m, stdin) == set(tuple(path) for path in generate_all_simple_paths(n, m, stdin))
postconditions.description: The set of all simple paths is generated by exploring all possible paths in the graph (tree + extra edges) without revisiting nodes, including paths of length 1 (single nodes).

postconditions.expression: len(all_simple_paths(n, m, stdin)) == sum(2**k for k in range(0, n)) if m == 0 else True
postconditions.description: For m=0 (no extra edges), the number of simple paths is the sum over all nodes of 2^k where k is the depth of the node in the tree (including single-node paths), which simplifies to 3^n - 1 for a complete binary tree with n nodes (but exact formula depends on tree structure).
